subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for existing ownerless rows, leaving operator or non-plugin clients as the recovery path?
rationale: This intentionally strengthens cross-plugin isolation while stopping a legacy plugin-runtime workflow that previously succeeded, so tests cannot determine the repository's desired security-versus-upgrade policy.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Require exact plugin-owner equality, treat ownerless legacy rows as operator-managed, and require deployed proof before merge.

options.title: Add operator migration first
options.body: Define and test an explicit operator or doctor recovery path for assigning or replacing legacy ownership before enforcing the rejection.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Continue allowing plugin-runtime patches of ownerless rows, accepting a weaker and potentially adoptable ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Require exact plugin-owner equality, treat ownerless legacy rows as operator-managed, and require deployed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the gateway session architecture and upgrade contract across the central storage and lifecycle boundaries.
